entry.title: Phantom Drive
entry.summary:
Vendor: Lab401
Type:
Price: 49.95

To properly protect your data, just encrypting isn't enough. Evidence of encryption can lead to suspicion or a legal obligation to decrypt. To be truly secure, your encrypted data also needs to be hidden.

The Phantomdrive is a secure, portable device that encrypts and hides your data.

When initally plugged in, it presents a standard USB drive. When authenticated, a previously undetectable, encrypted partition is mounted.

All data written is encrypted and decrypted transparently and securely using the drive's onboard hardware AES module. Your password is never stored in memory, and no software or drivers are required - everything is handled on device.

The Phantomdrive uses microSD cards for storage; users can easily swap cards to use several encrypted archives with just one device.

PROTECT & HIDE

Data are encrypted on-device with AES-256. When un-authorised, the encrypted partition is undetectable.

EASY TO USE

No complicated configuration. No drivers or software required. Works cross-platform: just plug it in.

OPEN-SOURCE & AUDITABLE

Source-code and schematics are on Github for your inspection, customisation and development.

What's included

  • 1x Phantomdrive
  • 2x Case sets
  • MicroSD card is not included!

Technical resources

  • Latest Firmware
  • Web Flasher
  • Getting Started Guide
  • Phantomdrive Repository

IMPORTANT ⚠️ Update your firmware

The PhantomDrive is delivered with firmware version 1.2. We highly recommend flashing v1.3 which adds some ease-of-use / quality-of-life updates, including automatic initial SD card formatting and preparation.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I authenticate / unlock the device?

Create a text-file that contains password:MyVerySecurePassword (Where "MyVerySecurePassword" is a long, secure password of your choice). The Phantomdrive monitors the default filesystem - when it sees this trigger, it reads the password, derives the AES256 key and remounts the hidden partition.

Why is this better than VeraCrypt?

VeraCrypt has two types of partitions: hidden, or visible.

  • Visibile partitions can be detected: an adversary knows that you have encrypted data. Many government, customs and law-enforcement agencies can legally compel you provide keys for encrypted data. When locked, the Phantomdrive works as a standard 8GB USB-drive. The encrypted partition is undetectable until you choose to reveal it.
  • VeraCrypt's hidden partitions are complicated to setup and easy to break. Likewise, they are somewhat impractical for portable drives - you must use the VeraCrypt software to unencrypt, mount, and unmount.

Why does Phantomdrive use microSD cards?

MicroSD cards provide more flexibility: users can easily swap between encrypted microSD cards without needing to purchase multiple Phantomdrives.

What happens if someone removes the microSD card?

The data on the microSD cards are encrypted - removing the card does not reveal your data.

Introduction

The PandwaRF Rogue Pro is a pocket-sized all-in-one multi-frequency RF remote sniffing/capture/decrypting/cloning solution, that supports all types of modulation, encryption and both fixed and rolling-codes.

The Rogue Pro has been specifically engineered to meet and exceed the requirements of the pentesters, security auditors and law-enforcement users. Its use case is simple: capture and replicate any remote control. While it is designed to operate autonomously, users retain full control over all aspects of the device's operation via the Android application.

Product Overview

The Rogue Pro can capture across all standard world-wide remote control frequencies (300MHz - 950MHz). When setup, it will automatically scan, capture, demodulate and label any matching signals for rapid processing via the application.

Rolling-codes are handled via "Kaiju", the Rogue Pro's dedicated online cracking platform. Effortlessly decrypt and decode all elements of a captured signal (brand / model / serial number / sync counter / cipher text / etc), and even transform signals (ie, change a "CLOSE DOOR" signal into an "OPEN DOOR" signal)

The Rogue Pro can also brute force targets, leveraging a highly optimised brute-force, zero-delay engine that results in 30x faster cracking over non-optimised devices.

For pentesters and professional users the Rogue Pro has functionality vital for field operations: pause & resume cracking and capture, ensuring that an interrupted operation is not a wasted operation.

Once a target has been cracked, the Rogue Pro acts as a clone of the original remote control - all signal transmissions, even rolling codes are supported: no more desynchronised target devices.

The Rogue Pro is closely integrated with the PandwaRF Maurauder, PandwaRF's autonomous, covert signal "dead drop" capture device. Data can be exported as JSON from the Marauder to the Rogue Pro easily via the Android Application - making it ideal for coordination and cooperation between teams.

THE BUMP KEY KIT YOU CAN TRUST

Key "Bumping" seems like magic: insert a specially crafted key into a lock, turn the key and hit it with a hammer - and the lock opens.

While the principles of key bumping are proven, in-the-field success depends heavily on the orchestration of several elements to be effective. Crucial to performance is the percussive tool: not enough force, the key displaces the key pins, rather than communicating the inertia through to the driver pins. Too much force can damage the lock and key, and also transmit lateral shock, which hinders pin movement.

Likewise, having the right bump keys makes all the difference. Lock profiles are different in different countries; too many keys becomes time-consuming, too-few keys is frustrating.
